title: Studio Ghibli
subtitle: every Ghibli film in release order, built around Miyazaki's
blurb: 26 films in release order. The 12 Miyazaki directed are the spine; the rest are marked with who made them.
paceLabel: the films Miyazaki did not direct
notes: The 12 films he directed are tier 1 and are what a finish date paces you through — about 22 hours. The other 14 are tier 2, each marked with its director, and sit outside the timeline unless you tick the box under the bar.
Two of them are not Ghibli films.

The Castle of Cagliostro was Miyazaki's first feature, made at Tokyo Movie Shinsha in 1979. Nausicaa came in 1984, before the studio existed — and did well enough that the studio was founded to make what came next.
Two more were made for television.

Ocean Waves and Earwig and the Witch were produced for broadcast rather than for cinemas, and both only reached Japanese screens afterwards. They are feature-length Ghibli films all the same, and are marked.
Bar widths are runtimes, read from each film's own article.

Every bar is the runtime printed in that film's own Wikipedia infobox, which is where a length keeps the name of the version it belongs to. 25 of the 26 have one; Ocean Waves was made for television and its article carries no film infobox, so its figure stays Wikidata's. The generator refuses to build without a runtime for every row.
Titles and years from Wikipedia's List of Studio Ghibli works; directors and release dates from Wikidata; runtimes from each film's own Wikipedia article.
